newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Commodity Price Index rises in July - ANZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ Commodity Price Index rises in July - ANZ.

text.p: The average New Zealand dollar price of the country's commodity exports rose 1.7 percent in July 1996 following a 5.9 percent fall in June, ANZ Banking Group (New Zealand) Ltd said on Wednesday.
The corresponding average world price of New Zealand's commodity exports also rose in July by 3.0 percent, compared with a 6.9 percent fall in June.

The New Zealand dollar index rose to 100.6 in July from 99.0 in June, down 10.4 percent on an annual basis, while the world price index rose to 122.3 from 118.8 over the same period, down 4.5 percent annually.
ANZ said its commodity price index registered an annual fall of 10.4 percent, compared with a fall of 14 percent in the year to June.

The New Zealand dollar strengthened against the U.S. and Australian dollars and the British pound during July, which meant that the improvement in the NZ price index (1.7 percent) was less marked than in the world price index (3.0 percent).

ANZ said the commodities which made a positive contribution to the rise included wool, fish, skim milk powder, sawn timber and skins. Prices for wood pulp, aluminium and beef continued to fall over the month.
On an annual basis, the general fall in prices had affected a majority of commodities, with only lamb, skins and apples showing a marked improvement in NZ dollar prices compared with a year ago.
